original_test_intent: Verify that the exact approved BF4 high-speed cable can be disconnected/reconnected once under its qualified service procedure, remains undamaged and correctly routed/latched, and restores the same BF4 endpoint and link without new faults.
original_method: Bind the BF4 cable PN/serial/length, both board/port endpoints, direction/keying, latch and bend-radius route; capture photos plus BF4 device/link/error baseline; isolate power as required; a qualified ESD-protected technician services only that cable once, without pulling by the cable body or forcing the latch; restore power/readiness and prove endpoint identity, expected link state and clean error counters/logs.
manual_activity: A qualified hardware technician inspects and services the single approved BF4 cable under its connector, ESD, bend-radius and power controls.
required_inputs: BF4 cable PN/serial/length and exact source/destination board-port mapping
Direction/keying, latch, minimum bend radius and routing drawing
Vendor disconnect/reconnect, ESD and required power-isolation procedure
Expected BF4 endpoint/device, firmware/driver, link speed/width/state and error limits
safety_requirements: Release the specified latch and handle connector housing; never pull or twist the cable body
Use the vendor-required power state and ESD controls before touching endpoints
Label and photograph both endpoints and route before disconnecting
Stop on bent pins, latch damage, keying mismatch, resistance, bend violation, missing endpoint, degraded link or new errors
No repeated cycling or automatic retry
agent_execution_scope: Validate cable/endpoints, service controls and the BF4 link oracle
Collect immutable pre/post endpoint, link/error outputs and operator photos
Correlate action timestamps and discrepancies without assessing tactile condition
Do not handle the cable, authorize live work, clear logs, reuse CX9 evidence or decide verdict
engineer_actions: Approve exact BF4 cable and endpoint-port pair plus one service cycle
Approve power/ESD/latch/bend-radius procedure, link/error criteria and recovery
Review physical/electronic evidence and decide PASS, FAIL, or BLOCKED

review_improvement: Replaces generic component handling with a BF4-cable-specific endpoint, connector and link-restoration contract.
independent_technical_reasoning: A BF4 cable can appear seated while its latch is incomplete, route exceeds bend limits, endpoints are swapped or the link returns degraded. The row therefore needs a two-ended identity and route, not the CX9 neighbors' evidence. The physical action remains human-only; the automation contribution is limited to correlating the same BF4 endpoint and link/error state before and after one controlled service cycle.
